title: iCloud Photos is stuck, paused or never finishes
symptom: Status says Syncing paused, Uploading N items for days, or Preparing... forever.

steps.text: Plug in, join stable Wi-Fi, turn off Low Power Mode and Low Data Mode, keep the Mac awake.
Check iCloud storage is not full (System Settings > Apple ID > iCloud) and Apple System Status shows iCloud Photos green.
Scroll to the very bottom of All Photos and read the status line. Note the number of items.
List the exact files that have not uploaded.
steps.why: One bad picture can hold the queue.

steps.text: Check the Photos log for sync errors and see what they mean.
Optional: see the raw sync errors.
Restart the Mac. Wait a few hours before trying anything else.
steps.why: Large libraries take hours or days.

steps.text: Only if still stuck AND originals are all on this Mac: toggle iCloud Photos off then on (Photos > Settings > iCloud).
steps.why: With Optimize Storage on, turning it off can delete full-size local copies. Check Download Originals first.

identify: Shoebox 'Pending uploads' lists each file and why it may be stuck.
Photos > Library > the 'Unable to Upload' view lists items Apple gave up on.
prevention: Do big imports on wired or strong Wi-Fi with the Mac on power.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: 'Unable to Upload' / 'Couldn't sync N items'
symptom: A banner or album lists items Photos could not send to iCloud.

steps.text: List the stuck files with likely cause (empty file, wrong extension, huge, odd type).
In Photos open the Unable to Upload view. Select the items.
File > Export > Export Unmodified Original into a new folder.
steps.why: Edits and keywords are lost on re-import, so note them if they matter.

steps.text: Run the Health check on that export folder to catch broken files, wrong extensions and bad dates before re-importing.
Convert videos Photos cannot read (set up for you, preview first).
Delete the originals from Photos, empty Recently Deleted, then import the exported files again.
steps.why: Only after you confirm the export folder has every file.

steps.text: If a file still fails, remove stray flags that block import.

identify: File name, size and date for each item from Shoebox 'Pending uploads'.
prevention: Avoid unusual formats and multi-GB videos in the main library.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Ghost, orphan or phantom files
symptom: Photos reports lots of storage but you see few pictures, deleted pictures still count, or the library folder is bigger than expected.

steps.text: Back up first: copy the whole .photoslibrary package to another drive (Finder, hold Option to copy, or Time Machine).
steps.why: Every repair step below is safer with a copy.

steps.text: Run the Library audit: lists files on disk that Photos does not know (orphans) and items Photos lists but cannot find, with exact paths.
Open the CSV from the audit. Orphans: copy them somewhere safe (do not delete inside the package).
Quit Photos, then hold Option+Command while reopening it and choose Repair.
Run the audit again to see what changed.
Re-import real orphan files you want to keep from your safe copy.
Optional: size of the package versus what Photos reports.

identify: Shoebox Library audit: orphans by exact path, missing-by-database list, empty files, wrong extensions.
In iCloud-synced libraries, 'cloud only' items are normal and not counted as missing.
prevention: Never move or delete files inside the .photoslibrary package by hand.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Unsupported format, 'Unable to load', or won't open
symptom: A picture or video shows a grey tile, 'Unable to Load Photo or Video', or fails to import.

steps.text: Run the Health check on the folder: it finds broken files, wrong extensions and unsupported types.
Check what a file really is.
If the extension is wrong, rename it to match (Shoebox Health can fix this in bulk).
Repair wrong file endings in bulk (preview first).
For unsupported RAW or video, convert it (Preview, ffmpeg, or the camera maker's tool) and import the converted copy; keep the original.
Update macOS: newer releases add camera and codec support.

identify: Shoebox Health check lists each file and what is wrong with it.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Import fails: 'Unknown Error', 'Operation not permitted'
symptom: Photos or Shoebox's Send to Photos reports errors for some or all files.

steps.text: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access: switch on Photos and Shoebox. Also Photos and Files-and-Folders / Removable Volumes if the files are on a drive.
Run the Health check to find empty or damaged files before importing.
Look at one failing file.
Clear quarantine and extended flags.
Import from the Mac's own drive, not a network share. Try a small batch first.
Watch the Photos log while retrying; Shoebox explains each error.
Retry sending in small, verified batches (set up for you, preview first).

identify: The failing path appears in Console lines; Shoebox pulls file names out of the log for you.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Library locked, won't open, or crashes
symptom: 'Library is locked or you do not have permissions', error 5600, error 41013, Photos hangs on launch.

steps.text: Back up first: copy the whole .photoslibrary package to another drive (Finder, hold Option to copy, or Time Machine).
steps.why: Every repair step below is safer with a copy.

steps.text: Library health check: format of the drive, permissions, free space, database state.
If the library is on an external drive: it must be APFS or Mac OS Extended (Journaled), connected directly, with 'Ignore ownership on this volume' ticked in Get Info.
Finder > Get Info on the library > Sharing & Permissions: your user = Read & Write, then Apply to enclosed items.
See owners and flags.
Quit Photos, hold Option+Command while opening it, and choose Repair.
If repair fails: make a new empty library (hold Option, Create New). If that works, the old one is damaged: import its originals folder into the new one in batches.

identify: Not file specific for lock/format errors; the repair log lists damaged items.
prevention: Keep a Time Machine backup of the library.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Copying or moving a library fails (error -36)
symptom: Finder says some data can't be read or written, or a copy stops partway.

steps.text: Disk Utility > First Aid on the source and the destination.
Remove stray resource files.
Use Shoebox's copy: it retries, skips unreadable files, and lists exactly which ones.
Make sure the destination is APFS or Mac OS Extended, not FAT32/ExFAT.

identify: Shoebox's copy report lists each file it could not read, by path.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Photos is slow, hot, or the disk fills up
symptom: photolibraryd, mediaanalysisd or photoanalysisd use lots of CPU or disk for days.

steps.text: Leave the Mac on power and awake overnight; after a big import analysis can take days.
Check the log for a crash loop on one item.
See the cache size.
If huge: quit Photos, delete the contents of that Caches folder, restart (it rebuilds).
Update macOS; many analysis bugs are fixed in point releases.

identify: Activity Monitor > photolibraryd > Open Files and Ports shows the file being worked on.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Export fails or 'Unknown Error'
symptom: Export stops, or says it completed with errors.

steps.text: Photos > Settings > iCloud: choose Download Originals (or right-click items > Download), wait for it to finish.
Library audit shows items whose original is not on disk.
Export 'Unmodified Original' rather than edited versions.
Export a few at a time to find the one that fails; that one is the damaged item.

identify: Failing items are the ones the export names; the audit lists those without a local original.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Shared Album won't take items
symptom: 'There was an error adding the selected items.'

steps.text: Turn Live Photo off on the failing items and try again.
Wait until analysis finishes after a big import.
Export and re-import the item, then share.

identify: The items that fail when added one by one.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Shoebox or another app can't see Photos
symptom: 'Not authorized', Operation not permitted, or an automation prompt never appears.

steps.text: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos / Automation / Full Disk Access: switch the app on.
Reset a stuck permission, then reopen the app and allow again.
Re-run the Photos log check.

identify: Not file specific.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Camera import corrupts or changes files
symptom: Checksum of the imported file differs from the card.

steps.text: Turn off 'Delete items after import'.
Compare the card copy and the imported copy.
Copy the card to a folder with Image Capture or Finder first, then import from there.
Format the card only after you have verified the copy.

identify: The files whose checksums differ.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: iPhone/iPad: 'Something Went Wrong' or won't load full quality
symptom: Pictures stay blurry or show an error on the device.

steps.text: Restart the device and toggle Airplane Mode.
Free device storage and update iOS.
Check Apple System Status for iCloud Photos.
Open the same picture on a Mac or iCloud.com: if it loads there, the cloud copy is fine.

identify: The picture you tapped.
provenance: supplied CSVs (AI-generated) + general macOS knowledge; not yet checked against Apple pages or real Console output

title: Photos analysis never starts / sync engine seems stuck for days
symptom: Nothing analysed (no people, places or Duplicates), cloudphotod uses a lot of CPU for a day or more, log shows ReadyForCPL or the same lines repeating.

steps.text: First, give it time: a first sync of a large library takes days to weeks. A steady heartbeat in the log is not proof it is working.
steps.why: Measured example: the first upload of 464,079 items finished by itself after about 16 days.

steps.text: Start the Sync meter and Live watch, and press 'Check the sync engine backlog'.
Press 'Check the sync engine backlog' again several hours later. Rows consumed? Then it is working. Exactly the same count while the store grows? It is looping.
steps.why: Decisive test from the reported case: 4,254,025 rows both times, 35 hours apart, while writing 734 MB.

steps.text: In the Live watch cards, read the targets in 'updated targets' lines: identical ones repeating means a loop, not progress.
Capture what cloudphotod is doing (keep the output for Apple).
steps.why: Highest-value single diagnostic in the reported case.

steps.text: Restart the Mac and re-measure. If the loop returns, note that it did.
Optional, untried in the reported case: restart the sync helper once (it restarts itself).
steps.why: Temporary reset only; do not repeat it in a loop.

steps.text: If it persists: build a fresh library from iCloud on another Mac and see whether it reproduces. If it does, it is account-side: escalate to Apple Support with your measurements (row counts, targets, sample file).
Keep the old library/drive until everything is verified.

identify: Engine store: <library>/resources/cpl/cloudsync.noindex/storage/store.cloudphotodb (no file extension).
transientPullRepository row count is the backlog.
prevention: Do not merge many libraries and create thousands of albums before turning on iCloud Photos.
provenance: David's own investigation (handover brief, 2026-10-03): measured on one ~595k-asset library, macOS/Photos version not recorded; measurements are real but from one library, so treat steps as well-supported leads

title: Is everything really in iCloud? Counts don't match
symptom: The Mac, iPhone and iCloud.com show different numbers of photos and videos.

steps.text: Get the library's own breakdown: visible, hidden, burst frames, shared library, trashed, photos vs videos.
On the iPhone read Photos > Albums > Utilities (Hidden, Recently Deleted) and the totals at the bottom of All Photos. Compare like with like.
On iCloud.com note the photos and videos totals. Expect small differences; look for large or one-sided ones.
List the files the library itself says have not uploaded.
Know the limits: the Mac's own belief about 'in iCloud' can be wrong, so different definitions gave 1, 364 and 2,052 in the reported case. Do not quote a single number as the answer.
steps.why: Also, .m4v files can be counted as photos on the Mac.

steps.text: For ground truth request a copy of your data: privacy.apple.com > Request a copy of your data > iCloud Photos. It takes days, so start it early.
Keep the old library or drive until you have checked.

identify: Spot check a few days and a few albums in each place; a uniform 1.5% gap is invisible at day level.
provenance: David's own investigation (handover brief, 2026-10-03): measured on one ~595k-asset library, macOS/Photos version not recorded; measurements are real but from one library, so treat steps as well-supported leads

title: Repeating CloudKit 'Unknown Item' errors for shared albums
symptom: Logs show CKError 11/2003 'Unknown Item' for SharedCollection-… zones many times an hour.

steps.text: Check the log and read which zone ids are failing.
Compare the shared albums listed on iCloud.com with those in the Photos sidebar. Look for ones present on one side only.
On iCloud.com open each missing album, Select All, Save to Library so the photos are kept, then delete the album.
Wait days, not minutes: in the reported case the errors stopped several days later. Do not contact Apple until then.
steps.why: One wrong call in the reported case was declaring this permanent after two days.

identify: The SharedCollection-<UUID> in the log; match by album name on iCloud.com.
provenance: David's own investigation (handover brief, 2026-10-03): measured on one ~595k-asset library, macOS/Photos version not recorded; measurements are real but from one library, so treat steps as well-supported leads

title: After Repair Library: huge .aside or -wal files, counts changed
symptom: Repair finished, but the library folder is huge or the photo count changed.

steps.text: Quit Photos and restart the Mac; a huge -wal file often shrinks on its own.
Run the Library audit to check files on disk against the database.
Get the count breakdown and compare with your phone.
Only when counts match and the library opens, consider deleting Photos.sqlite.aside. Keep a backup until you are sure.
steps.why: It is the old database; deleting it cannot be undone.

identify: Finder > Show Package Contents > database/ shows sizes.
provenance: David's own investigation (handover brief, 2026-10-03): measured on one ~595k-asset library, macOS/Photos version not recorded; measurements are real but from one library, so treat steps as well-supported leads
